trans-unit.target: This campaign, its medias, its counterparts, its draws and the contributions it received are deleted for good. Nothing brings them back.
This campaign leaves the listing for the recycle bin, keeping everything it holds. It is restored from there.
Everything the form's fields do not say is written in blocks, with the same editor the site's pages are composed with.
The goal, the dates, the presentation and the author: what a campaign is before it has anything to offer.
What a contributor gets in return for their gift, with its amount and, where there is one, the number of copies available.
Once the draw has been filmed, the video goes on the lottery or, if the file is too heavy, on the campaign with a YouTube address.
A draw date and prizes. Tickets are sold like counterparts, and the draw happens on the lottery's public page.
The photographs and videos of the public page: a campaign nobody sees is a campaign nobody funds.
A news entry is published from the campaign's public page, by its author. It is corrected and removed here, on the campaign's own screen.
A campaign is written masked: out of the listing, of the sitemap and of the basket, its page answering 404. Look at it as a visitor will, then take the mask off.
The same campaign said in another language: its texts alone belong to it, the goal, the currency and the dates being the same everywhere.
Deleting takes two gestures and two screens: the first is undone from the recycle bin, the second is not undone at all.

The "Blocks" section, at the very bottom of the form. Texts, pictures, buttons, tables: the same as a page of the site's - plus a "Crowdfunding" category. Three of those are this campaign's own and read it rather than repeating it: Campaign medias, Campaign counterparts and Campaign lottery.
The blocks show on the public page, below the presentation and the counterparts.
The pencil, on the row of the campaign to fill in.
A fourth block, "Campaigns", is not placed here but on an ordinary page of the site: it lists the open campaigns there with their progress, and keeps itself up to date.
A campaign's blocks are composed on its sheet, below the fields describing it.
Who carries the project. The name, the presentation and the website appear together on the page: a contributor gives to somebody, not to a pot.
The campaign only takes contributions between these two dates. Before, and after, its counterparts can no longer be added to the basket.
The opening text, at the top of the public page. Say in a few lines what you want to do and why; the detail is composed further down, in blocks.
The campaign is online as soon as it exists, and visible between its two dates. The parcours that follow fill it in: its pictures, its counterparts, its lottery.
The amount to reach. It is what the public page's gauge compares the contributions already received to.
The button above the list opens an empty form. It carries everything: the campaign, its media, its counterparts, its lottery and its blocks.
Every campaign of the site is listed here, the one ending latest first.
It fills itself in from the title. Once the campaign has been shared, leave it alone: the links already out there would stop working.
It is the name the campaign appears under everywhere: in the list, on its page, in the basket and in the emails sent to contributors.
The "Counterparts" section. Give it a title, an amount and a description: it is what a contributor reads before choosing.
The counterpart is added to the basket like any other item. The shop is what takes the money: this bundle never handles it.
The pencil, on the row of the campaign the counterpart belongs to.
A counterpart once added folds onto its title. Open it: the price, the limited quantity and the expected delivery are all inside.
A counterpart belongs to a campaign and is created on its sheet: there is no counterparts screen.
A limited quantity takes the counterpart off sale once it runs out, and the basket refuses to order more than what is left. Leave zero not to limit it.
The winners have already had their email, sent at the moment of the draw. The video is what everybody else sees: it remains to be announced, by hand, on social networks.
The pencil, on the row of the campaign whose lottery has just been drawn.
The "Lottery" section, the one you have just drawn. Open it: its "Videos" field is folded up inside.
The draw's video goes on the campaign carrying the lottery, like everything else.
Its "Videos" field only takes an uploaded file. The video then shows under the prizes, on the draw's own page, where contributors go looking for it.
For a file too heavy: publish it on YouTube, then paste its address into the campaign's videos, in the "Media" section. It is the only one of the two fields taking an address.
The "Lottery" section. Tick "Enable" and set the draw's date: the draw button stays greyed out until it has passed.

The draw itself does not happen here: it takes place on the lottery's public page, at the date set, and you alone see the button there. Film it: the "Film and publish a lottery draw" procedure says how, and why there is no second take.
The pencil, on the row of the campaign carrying the lottery.
A lottery once added folds onto its title. Open it: "Enable", the identifier, the draw's date and the prizes are all inside.
A lottery belongs to a campaign: its tickets are contributions, and its draw rewards those who gave.
One prize per rank, from the first to the last. A ticket only wins once: a ticket already drawn is taken out of the draws that follow.
One image, the one the catalogue and the social networks show of the campaign. It is shown whole, never cropped.
The public page shows your pictures. Nothing more to publish: what is saved is online.
The pencil, on the row of the campaign to illustrate.
One image, the one the campaign page opens on, printed under its title.
A campaign's pictures go on its own sheet: it is a single form, where everything composing it holds together.
The "Media" section. Every picture added shows on the public page, in the order you put them in. The first one is the one seen first.
Just below. A campaign video takes an uploaded file or, more simply, a YouTube address: that is the way to go for a heavy file.
The correction shows on the campaign's page at once. Publishing a new entry is the public page and not this screen: see the "Publish a campaign news entry" procedure.
Open the campaign holding the news entry to go back over.
A news entry folds onto its title. Open it: the title and the text are inside, and are gone back over like any other field.
Every news entry of the campaign is there, the most recent first. It is also where a news entry is removed from.
News entries belong to a campaign and are gone back over on its screen: there is no news screen.
It can be masked again at any time by the same switch: it leaves the listing and its page answers 404 once more, without losing anything it holds.
Back on the listing, the pencil opens the campaign's form.
Just under the title. Turn it off and the campaign joins the listing, the sitemap and the basket, and its page answers.
Every campaign of the site, opened or not: the one to publish is among them.
The eye button opens the campaign's own page in a new tab, as the visitor will read it - the block cache set aside, and a banner saying it is not open yet.
The code leading to the public page, to print on a poster or a flyer.
The save brought you back to the listing. Reopen the campaign with the pencil: the QR code is only drawn on its own form.
The preview button has given way to an external link: the campaign's page is now the one everybody reads.
The button opens the campaign straight into the first language to translate. It only shows where the site declares more than one language.
The name and the website stay the same in every language: only the presentation is translated.
Each counterpart is translated here, then the news and the prizes. Nothing is added or removed there: it would be in every language at once.
The campaign's story. Whatever stays between brackets shows in the writing language.
The campaign reads in this language at its translated address.
A translation starts from the list of campaigns.
The tabs move from one language to another, the first being the one the campaign was written in.
The title between brackets is the writing language's own. Until it is translated, the campaign is not announced to search engines in this language.
Above the list, the Recycle bin button shows the campaigns taken out of it, and only those.
The box button on the campaign's row. It asks for a confirmation, then takes the campaign out of the listing: its page answers 410 and it keeps everything it holds.
As long as a campaign sits in the recycle bin it can come back. Emptying it is a decision of its own, taken row by row.
The campaign to remove is in this list.

The last gesture, and the only one that undoes nothing: the campaign, its medias, its counterparts, its draws and the contributions it received go for good, and a gone redirect is left at its address.
Brings the campaign back with everything it still holds. It comes back masked, its own switch having been turned on when it was trashed.
Counterparts kept, contributors have already subscribed to them: %counterparts%
The campaign is deleted for good, with everything it held.
The campaign is restored, masked: open it once its page is composed again.
Lotteries kept, tickets have already been sold on them: %lotteries%
Short id to link a menu entry to this section (e.g. "crowdfunding"). Empty = derived from the title.
The campaigns open to read, each on its card with its funding bar and its deadline, kept up to date on their own.
The campaign's counterparts, as unfoldable rows, with a highlighted tier and the remaining stock.
The slug of the counterpart to frame, left empty to highlight none.
The link sits at the end of the title line. Both fields are needed: either alone shows nothing.
The campaign's draws and their prizes, read from the lotteries themselves.
Show the number of allocated tickets
The campaign's medias in a slider, with nothing to upload again.
Reminder of the counterparts you picked:
Thank you for your contribution and your trust!
These texts belong to this language alone. Everything else - goal, currency, dates, slug - is the same everywhere and is written on the screen the campaign was written on.
We will follow up on this very quickly.
Compose the rest of the page
Open the campaign to the public
Drop the video on the lottery
List of all crowdfunding campaigns. Create, edit or delete a campaign: goal, dates, presentation, counterparts, news, medias and its lottery.
I'm contributing for the next smiley!

Only those who left a message appear here
This campaign is not open yet: you are the only one reading this page.
Paints the section as a full-width flat - the text, dividers and buttons it holds invert automatically to stay readable.
Only some tickets appear in the animation, but, obviously, all of them are used for the drawing.
EITHER a Youtube ID OR a video file below
The funding is over: these counterparts are no longer available.

The image standing for the campaign wherever it is named but not opened: the catalogue card and the link shared on the social networks. Shown whole, never cropped. One per campaign.
The image the campaign page opens on, printed under its title. The catalogue and the social networks show the cover above. One per campaign.
A masked campaign appears neither in the listing, nor in the sitemap, nor in the basket, and its page answers 404: it is read through the Preview action.
Add items WITHOUT media/files and then add them afterwards, otherwise it doesn't work.
Some counterparts entitle you to a number of lottery tickets, the prizes of which are listed below.
By contributing to a crowdfunding campaign, you were eligible for the lottery tickets below:
You entered a crowdfunding lottery and won!
To print on a poster or a flyer: it leads to the public page of the campaign.
The images the page's slider runs through. To show one both as the opening image and in the slider, upload it on each of the two fields.
